title: Germplasm Preservation, Cryopreservation, and Clean Stock
objective: Design a redundant germplasm system that connects identity, health, preservation method, recovery, and periodic verification.
coreScience: Germplasm preservation protects genetic resources against crop loss, contamination, equipment failure, mislabeling, and biological decline. No single method protects against every risk.

Living mothers are accessible but exposed to pests, pathogens, space limits, and continuous management. In vitro slow-growth collections reduce space but require aseptic maintenance and passage. Seeds preserve populations rather than exact heterozygous clones. Cryopreservation can store shoot tips at liquid-nitrogen temperatures and reduce active growth, but recovery is protocol- and genotype-dependent.

A cannabis droplet-vitrification study recovered shoot tips from three cultivars with substantial differences among cryoprotectant treatments and cultivars. Preservation success must include post-recovery growth, identity, health, and phenotype—not only tissue survival.
cultivationRelevance: Maintain geographically or operationally independent backups. Link every accession to provenance, clone or seed identity, health status, preservation method, storage location, inventory, recovery test, and responsible owner.

measureAndRecord.requirement: Accession ID; genotype/chemotype; provenance; health tests; storage method and location; passage or regeneration date; cryoprotectant/protocol where used; recovery; identity and phenotype checks; loss events.

misconceptions: One mother plant is a germplasm bank.
Frozen tissue is automatically recoverable and true-to-type.
Seed storage preserves an exact elite female clone.
evidenceLimits: Cryopreservation is specialist work requiring validated facilities, hazardous-material controls, oxygen-deficiency safeguards, and genotype-specific recovery. This lesson does not provide a cryogenic procedure. ‘Clean stock’ requires ongoing organism-specific testing and identity control.
crossLinks: THC-ENC-141–160 for identity/genetic fidelity; THC-ENC-173–179 for health/testing/tissue culture; THC-ENC-301–340 for pathogen and biosecurity controls.
